primary_report.title: How employment is changing at Anthropic

verified_claims: Junior share of technical hires declined from 27% to 9%; junior share of technical-department employees declined from 21% to 14% since early 2025.
Overall technical hiring continued growing in absolute terms. Falling shares are not a count of jobs eliminated or evidence that hiring stopped.
Hiring assessments increasingly emphasize autonomy and judgment.
The report notes that protections for current employees do not benefit people who are never hired.
source_claims_not_carried_into_draft: A blanket announcement that Anthropic will not hire newcomers is not supported.
A guaranteed succession gap in three to five years is the commentator’s forecast, not a measured report result.
Agent work hours are runtime with a distinct denominator, not productivity. Code commits are not overall engineering quality.
The 75% versus 28% forecast concerns respondents’ expectations for 2030, not measured current automation.
editorial_inference: Training pathways, bounded ownership and review of reasoning are the proposed perspective, not a tested company policy or reported research finding.
